# Set up Omarchy for Flisk

<tr><td>

Get your Omarchy computer ready for Flisk. You do this once. [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org/) is Arch Linux with Hyprland, so the usual Arch packages work. Run these in a [terminal](../start/words.md#terminal) (press Super+Enter to open one): copy each grey box, paste it and press Enter. A command that starts with `sudo` runs as the computer's administrator, so it asks for your password. Never written code? [Start here](../start/first-time.md).

**1. Node.js 22.12 or newer**, plus your app's own runtime. [Node.js](../start/words.md#nodejs) is a free program that Flisk runs on, and [npm](../start/words.md#npm) comes with it. If your app is written in something else, such as Python, install that too. For a small app, that is all you need: the [simplest path](../start/simplest.md) runs each [part of your app](../start/words.md#app-parts) as a normal program on your computer (your services run as local processes). This command installs Node.js and npm with `pacman`, Arch's own app installer:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed nodejs npm
```

**2. Only for bigger apps: Docker and Tilt.** You need these when your app has a [database](../start/words.md#database), one web address in front of all its parts (a gateway URL), or must run in the same [container](../start/words.md#container) you deploy. Check [Docker](../start/words.md#docker) with `docker info`: it prints Docker's details when Docker is installed and running. If it is missing:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed docker docker-compose
sudo systemctl enable --now docker.service
```

To run `docker` without `sudo`, follow Docker's [post-install steps](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/linux-postinstall/). Then install [Tilt](../start/words.md#tilt) 0.25+:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tilt-dev/tilt/master/scripts/install.sh \
  | bash
```

**3. Install Flisk and check your computer:**

```bash
npm install -g @flisk-sh/flisk
flisk doctor
```

The first line [installs](../start/words.md#install) Flisk with npm. The second, [`flisk doctor`](../start/words.md#flisk-doctor), checks only what your project uses and prints a fix for anything missing. To check that Flisk itself is installed, run `flisk --version`: it prints a version number.

Rather not install Node.js? [Install the prebuilt binary](../install/binary.md) instead: it needs nothing else.
